prompt: Analyze OSII/GSII buffer rates by country and bank with focus on the last 12 months. Emphasize country patterns, bank-level differences, and what objectives/risks these buffers address; avoid explaining tool mechanics. Be specific about which countries have higher/lower rates and notable bank-level variations. Write ONE paragraph of 6-7 sentences.
response: Over the last 12 months, OSII/GSII buffer rates have exhibited distinct country and bank-level patterns, reflecting varying regulatory environments and institutional risk profiles. Countries with more stringent capital requirements or perceived higher systemic risk, such as Germany and France, generally show higher average OSII/GSII buffers, indicating a proactive approach to absorbing potential shocks. Conversely, countries with lower systemic risk or more flexible regulatory frameworks, like Ireland or Portugal, tend to have lower average buffer rates. At the bank level, globally systemic important institutions (G-SIIs) consistently maintain higher buffers than other systemically important institutions (OSIIs) within the same country, a direct consequence of their larger footprint and greater potential impact. Notable variations exist even among G-SIIs in similar jurisdictions, suggesting differences in their specific business models, asset quality, and internal risk management practices. These elevated buffers primarily address the objective of enhancing financial system resilience by ensuring banks can absorb losses during periods of stress, thereby mitigating the risk of contagion and systemic collapse. Conversely, lower buffers might reflect a trade-off between capital efficiency and systemic risk mitigation, or a belief in the effectiveness of other supervisory tools.
